name: PulseSensor optical heart-rate sensor
description: World Famous Electronics' open-source optical heart-rate sensor (photoplethysmography): a green LED shines into a fingertip or earlobe, an APDS-9008 light sensor picks up the reflected light and an amplifier turns each pulse into an analog Signal that rests near Vdd/2 and rises with every heartbeat. Runs on 3.0-5.5 V, about 4 mA; the Signal swings up to Vdd, so power it from 3.3 V for a 3.3 V ADC. Not a medical device. Sold as: PulseSensor Kit / Pulse Sensor Amped by World Famous Electronics (PulseSensor.com, also Adafruit #1093 and SparkFun SEN-11574), 15.8 mm round sensor on a 24 in ribbon cable ending in three male header pins: black GND, red Vdd, purple Signal.
eli5: Rest your fingertip on the little heart-shaped light and it turns your pulse into a wiggly voltage your board can read and count.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, black wire (pin 1 of the ribbon).

pins.name: Vdd
pins.description: Supply, red wire (pin 2), 3.0-5.5 V, about 4 mA. Use 3.3 V on a 3.3 V board: the Signal can rise all the way to Vdd.

pins.name: Signal
pins.description: Analog pulse waveform, purple wire (pin 3): rests near Vdd/2 (1.65 V on 3.3 V) and rises with each heartbeat; datasheet range 0.3 V to Vdd. Connect to an ADC pin.

supplierQuery: PulseSensor pulse sensor amped heart rate
buildNotes: Power it from 3.3 V when the board's ADC is 3.3 V: the datasheet gives the Signal range as 0.3 V to Vdd, so on 5 V it can exceed a 3.3 V pin.
Identify the three leads by colour (black GND, red Vdd, purple Signal); reversing power can damage the sensor.
Stick a clear vinyl dot on the front and insulate the exposed parts on the back (hot glue, per the manual) before it touches skin.
Use light, steady pressure (the stabilizer ring or Velcro strap). Pressing hard flattens the pulse; movement and bright ambient light add noise.
On ESP32 use an ADC1 pin (ADC2 is unusable while Wi-Fi is on). Raspberry Pi has no ADC: use an ADS1115 or MCP3008.
Hobby/educational sensor, not a medical device.

driver.code:
# PulseSensor (World Famous Electronics, PulseSensor.com) optical heart-rate sensor, MicroPython driver.
# The sensor is a green LED + APDS-9008 light sensor + op-amp stage: its purple Signal wire is an
# analog photoplethysmogram (PPG) that rests near Vdd/2 and rises with each heartbeat
# (datasheet: output 0.3 V .. Vdd, typical Vdd/2). Power it from 3.3 V so Signal never exceeds 3.3 V.
import time
from machine import ADC, Pin


class PulseSensor:
    def __init__(self, signal, vref=3.3):
        self.adc = ADC(Pin(signal))
        try:
            self.adc.atten(ADC.ATTN_11DB)  # ESP32: full 0-3.3 V range
        except AttributeError:
            pass
        self.vref = vref

    def raw(self):
        """Raw ADC reading, 0..65535."""
        return self.adc.read_u16()

    def voltage(self):
        """Signal voltage in volts (about Vdd/2 = 1.65 V between beats on a 3.3 V supply)."""
        return self.adc.read_u16() * self.vref / 65535

    def bpm(self, beats=4, learn_ms=2000, timeout_ms=10000, period_ms=4):
        """Heart rate in beats per minute from the time between beats, or None if no clear pulse.

        Learns the waveform's low and high level first, then times `beats` intervals between
        rising crossings of a threshold at 60 % of that range (re-armed below 40 %),
        ignoring crossings closer than 250 ms (faster than 240 BPM)."""
        lo, hi = 65535, 0
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < learn_ms:
            v = self.adc.read_u16()
            lo = min(lo, v)
            hi = max(hi, v)
            time.sleep_ms(period_ms)
        if hi - lo < 2000:  # under about 0.1 V of swing: no finger / no usable pulse
            return None
        up = lo + (hi - lo) * 6 // 10
        down = lo + (hi - lo) * 4 // 10
        armed = False
        edges = []
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < timeout_ms:
            v = self.adc.read_u16()
            now = time.ticks_ms()
            if not armed and v < down:
                armed = True
            elif armed and v > up:
                armed = False
                if not edges or time.ticks_diff(now, edges[-1]) > 250:
                    edges.append(now)
                    if len(edges) > beats:
                        return 60000 * beats / time.ticks_diff(edges[-1], edges[0])
            time.sleep_ms(period_ms)
        return None
